brief.voice: a 24-year-old in their first full-time job

title: Unreal side hustle experience
body: I just finished my first month working as a freelance graphic designer on Upwork. I was skeptical at first but it's been a game changer. I've already paid off over $3,000 in student loans and built up some savings. The best part is that I get to work from home and choose my own projects. My employer doesn't care about the weird hours as long as the work gets done.

brief.angle: buying a used truck with high mileage

title: Used truck woes - 200k miles is a red flag no matter what they say.
body: I just bought my son his first car, a used truck from a private seller. It's an okay deal, but the seller claims it's been well maintained despite having over 200k miles on it. I'm not convinced. The engine is a little rough and I can already see some signs of wear on the interior. I feel like I'm taking a gamble on reliability. Anyone else have experience with high mileage vehicles? Help!

title: First good harvest in years after that brutal spring
body: Just got back from my fields and I'm relieved to say it's been a decent year. Had to replant half the wheat due to hail damage, but the corn is finally ready for harvest. Been farming this land since '82 and never had a season as tough as last spring was - we're talking floods, frost, and a late freeze. Glad to see some green again.

brief.voice: a 27-year-old who moved to a new city

title: Meal prep is overrated in a new city
body: I've been trying to get into meal prepping since moving to this new city but I'm starting to think it's not worth the hassle. Every week, I plan out my meals, make a big batch of something on Sunday night, and then end up eating the same old thing by Wednesday. It gets boring and doesn't save me as much time as I thought it would. Has anyone else found this to be true or am I just doing it wrong?

brief.angle: a phone battery that dies by noon
brief.ptype: sharing a practical tip that worked

title: My Phone Battery Never Dies Before Noon Anymore
body: I was getting frustrated with my phone battery dying by lunchtime every day. I changed a few things and now it lasts all day without needing to be charged again. First, I turned off Location Services for most of the apps that didn't need them. Then I set my screen brightness to automatic. Now I only charge it once in the morning and it makes it through the whole day.

brief.ptype: sharing a practical tip that worked

title: Using life insurance payouts to help aging parents financially
body: My mom had a term life policy she'd paid into for years. She passed away last year and we got a decent payout from the insurance company. We put it in her bank account, but our financial advisor suggested we could use it to pay off some of the medical bills she'd accumulated over time. It really helped us get that sorted out without having to dig into our own savings.

title: Winter tires made a huge difference in my daily commute.
body: I just moved to a new city that gets slammed with snow every winter. Last year I struggled to get to work on time, but this year I decided to invest in a set of winter tires for my trusty old Honda Civic. The difference is night and day - I can stop on a dime and stay safe on the roads. Worth every penny.

brief.voice: a 27-year-old who moved to a new city

title: Making picky kids eat healthy stuff: a mom's trick that worked for me
body: I've been living in this new city for 3 months now and my neighbor, who's a single mom, has been sharing some really helpful parenting tips. She swears by the 'involve them in the process' method when it comes to cooking dinner. Her kid is super picky but she lets him help with meal planning and grocery shopping. He gets to choose between 2-3 healthy options every week. So far, so good! My niece is a huge fan of making her own quesadillas.
